claim: LATS (MCTS over actions with real environment returns, an LM value and written reflections) beats ReAct, Reflexion, ToT and RAP at the same trajectory budget on the authors' own tests (HotPotQA EM 0.63 vs Reflexion 0.51 with GPT-3.5; HumanEval 83.8 vs 68.1; WebShop score 75.9 vs 64.2). Independent re-run (Kapoor 2024): LATS GPT-4 HumanEval 88.0 (82.3-91.5) at $134.50 vs published 92.7; warming-retry baseline 93.2 at $2.45; LATS evaluation dropped 4 problems and used partial tests.
agent_test: Run our S6 with a program-owned tree vs a reflect-retry loop at equal tokens on the same items; report CIs.

claim: The headline LATS gains are weakly supported: HotPotQA uses 100 questions and WebShop 50 tasks, one run, no confidence intervals, and HotPotQA search uses ground-truth feedback (oracle). No independent re-run of LATS numbers is in the evidence set. Confirmed independently: the HumanEval set was altered, and no run of LATS without the oracle exists (Karthikeyan shows self-reward gains vanish without ground truth).
agent_test: Re-run on 300+ items with 3 seeds and no oracle signal.

claim: The LATS gain over a strong baseline shrinks with a stronger model: HumanEval over Reflexion is +15.7 points with GPT-3.5 but +1.7 with GPT-4 (92.7 vs 91.0).
agent_test: Measure search-over-retry gain at two model strengths on our tasks.

claim: At matched sample counts, tree search beats best-of-N when sampling is wide: LATS n=5,k=50 0.63 vs ReAct best-of-250 0.42 and CoT-SC 0.40; LATS n=1 (no branching) 0.48. Budgets are matched in trajectories, not tokens; LATS used about 176k tokens per success vs RAP 210k. Contested: a web-task control (Koh) shows search over re-ranking at about equal calls (37.0 vs about 30), but on HumanEval simple retries match LATS accuracy at 1/55 of the cost (Kapoor).
agent_test: Compare at equal TOKENS including failed runs, not equal trajectories.

claim: The LM value function is the bottleneck. Removing the LM heuristic drops LATS HotPotQA from 0.63 to 0.37; in VisualWebArena a ground-truth value gives 43.5% vs 37.0% for the best LM value and 24.5% without search; self-consistency on the value raises 28.5 to 32.5 (n=5) to 37.0 (n=20).
agent_test: Swap in a checkable verifier for the LM value on a subset and measure the gap; vary value samples at fixed total tokens.

claim: Tree search with an LM value gives real but modest gains on live web agents, large only in relative terms: VWA 18.9 to 26.4, WebArena 15.0 to 19.2 (GPT-4o); absolute results stay under 27%. Gains are larger on medium tasks (+75% relative).
agent_test: Test on tasks where greedy fails but a retry exists; log gain by task difficulty.

claim: More search budget helps on web tasks with diminishing returns: VWA subset 24.5 (c=0), 32.0 (c=5), 37.0 (c=20); depth 5 and breadth 5 best. Whole-trajectory re-ranking plateaus near 30% at n=7. Depth/branch grid cells conflict between extractions; trust c07 (d2b5 35.0%).
agent_test: Sweep budget and report per-budget token cost.

claim: Self-correction without an external signal does not help and often hurts: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0. With oracle labels it helps (GPT-4 HotpotQA 49 to 59).
agent_test: Add a rule: revise only after an external check; compare with free self-revision.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Self-critique by the same LLM is an unreliable verifier; a sound external verifier is what makes iteration work. Game of 24: LLM-critic 3% vs sound verifier 36-38%; verifier false-positive 10.4%, false-negative 20.7%. Exception: Blocksworld self-critique rose 40 to 55.
agent_test: Give the verifier access to code/tools/checks; compare to prompt-only verifier.

claim: Self-repair is not clearly better than drawing fresh samples at equal budget (repair/i.i.d. ratio mostly 0.83-1.09); feedback quality is the limiter (human feedback 52.6% vs model feedback 33.3% on GPT-4 failures). Newer data: fixed task guidance matched feedback-driven retry in a 7B code-as-policy study (86.1% vs 85.3%), and resampling reached 68.3%.
agent_test: Compare revise-after-failure vs fresh resample at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection adds little once search is present: in LATS removing reflection costs only 0.05 (0.63 to 0.58) while Reflexion alone gains 0.19 over ReAct; with real tests Reflexion helps (Rust 0.60 to 0.68) but test false positives can reach 16.3% (MBPP).
agent_test: Ablate written reflections inside our tree at equal tokens.

claim: Tree search is only useful when the discriminator is accurate: Chen et al. find no significant gain over re-ranking or iterative correction below about 90% judge accuracy (GSM8K GPT-3.5 51.0 vs 47.6, McNemar p>0.05); with an oracle judge tree search 73.0 vs 64.1. Karthikeyan: on GSM8K self-reward selection scored .776/.469/.854/.685 vs random .751/.450/.864/.680 (4 models); on ToolTalk self-feedback MCTS lowered F1 (Sonnet3 .706 to .559). Koh: weaker value LLaVA 30.0 vs GPT-4o 37.0 vs ground truth 43.5.
agent_test: Measure our judge accuracy; only enable search above a threshold.

claim: Search with MCTS costs far more than sampling: Wu et al. show MCTS underperforms sampling-based methods at every budget with dozens of times more tokens; SWE-Search cost for GPT-4o rose $40.86 to $576 (about 14x) for +5.3 points.
agent_test: Always report accuracy at equal total tokens including failures.

claim: Verifier-guided breadth beats classic MCTS on math: REBASE with Llemma-7B beat Llemma-34B; Snell et al. find beam search helps on medium difficulty and hurts on easy questions at high budget, with little benefit on the hardest.
agent_test: Spend search only on medium-difficulty items; test on difficulty strata.

claim: Trained value models beat prompted ones by large margins, which a no-training agent cannot use: Game24 LLaMA-SFT 9.2 (prompted) vs 64.8 (trained value); Agent Q online search lifts OpenTable 81.7 to 95.4. At equal tokens on GSM8K, plain voting with a reward model often wins.
agent_test: Record as upper bound; skip.

claim: LM-simulated world models (RAP) help on small planning tasks but degrade with horizon: Blocksworld LLaMA-33B 1.00/0.86/0.26 for 2/4/6 steps; GPT-4 CoT beats RAP(10) at 6 steps (0.40 vs 0.26).
agent_test: Where real checks exist, prefer them over LM-simulated states.

claim: Search in code agents helps modestly across five models (+17 to +27% relative on SWE-bench Lite subset); the value function picks the correct solution 73% of the time and a discriminator debate 84%. No same-cost best-of-N baseline was run.
agent_test: Compare tree search vs equal-cost resampling with test-based selection.

claim: Large-sample resampling with a reliable verifier is a strong rival to tree search: SWE-bench Lite 15.9% at 1 sample to 56% at 250 samples (tests as verifier).
agent_test: Always include a best-of-N with the same verifier as the control.

claim: On code with real example tests, simple retry baselines match or beat LATS at a fraction of the cost: HumanEval GPT-4, 5 runs each, warming 93.2 ($2.45), retry 92.0 ($2.51), Reflexion 87.8 ($3.90), LATS 88.0 ($134.50).
agent_test: Run retry-with-temperature, reflect-retry and tree arms at equal dollars on code items with hidden tests.

claim: A prompted self-judge on the tree gives most of its gain only through the ground-truth check. Without ground truth, picking the top self-scored node is at or below random on 3 of 4 GSM8K models; majority vote over the nodes is the reliable readout (.883/.608/.905/.786 vs no search .813/.426/.866/.757).
agent_test: Use agreement across branches (or a real check) to pick the answer, not the judge's top score.

claim: Search on a task with open-ended steps can be net harmful with a self-judge: ToolTalk F1 fell for both Claude 3 models (Sonnet3 .706 to .559, Haiku3 .638 to .605).
agent_test: Add an off switch: compare tree with plain pass on a small calibration set before enabling.

claim: Backtracking in live web environments is implemented by reset-and-replay, and irreversible actions (e.g. placing an order) must be excluded or gated; LATS itself says reversion is not universal.
agent_test: Tag every operator reversible or irreversible; never expand irreversible ones.

claim: A cheap prompted gate on whether to branch can cut tree-search cost 75-85% on math with little accuracy change (BN-DP, 14 settings), but its self-consistency form was unstable in 1-4 settings; the one measured difficulty estimator for per-item gating (Snell) needs 2048 samples per question and was not charged.
agent_test: Test a prompted per-step branch gate on code and web tasks; log its cost.

claim: On a reasoning-era model (Qwen3-30B-A3B-2507) MCTS-style search gives small math gains (MATH500 79.25 to 80.60 to 82.09; AIME25 48.67 to 50.00 to 53.33) and a poorly matched tree can lose badly (ReST-MCTS AIME25 20.00). The DeepSeek-R1 report says native long reasoning allocates compute by difficulty and MCTS self-improvement failed.
agent_test: Re-test trees on the current model at its native thinking budget before building them in.

claim: Best-of-N over agents saturates early with an exact verifier (60-94% of the 100-agent gain by 20 agents), and a frontier model's flat curve leaves little variance to harvest; structure that raises the mean per sample beats more samples.
agent_test: Cap resamples; prefer a stronger single pass to a wider tree on easy items.

claim: Written feedback in retry loops may work as static guidance: in a 7B code-as-policy study feedback 85.3%, other-episode feedback and fixed template 86.1%, resampling 68.3% (+17.1 pp, CI +9.9 to +24.2); feedback lowered recovery on one task (82.5 vs 97.5).
agent_test: Include a fixed-hint arm and a plain-resample arm in every reflection ablation.

claim: A program-owned tree with the model filling small slots can let 7-8B models match flat loops on 70B (ReAcTree 8B about ReAct 70B, +25 pp GSR at equal size 70B), but at 7B a complex hierarchical prompt format hurt without good examples.
agent_test: Keep node prompts flat and short; test the same tree on a small and a large model.

claim: Value self-consistency helps a prompted value function: VWA subset 28.5 (single call), 32.5 (n=5), 37.0 (n=20), ground truth 43.5; no cost-matched comparison against extra branches exists.
agent_test: Run a cost-matched test: value samples vs branches at equal LM calls.
